clue.text: Celebrates dancing round piano, upright

indicators.note: round means the shuffled letters go around the piano symbol
dancing sets the letters of the word celebrates moving into a new order

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: Someone celebrates by dancing round a piano, specifically an upright one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upright' looks like a type of piano, but it is the definition in its moral sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An upright person is honest and decent, which is synonymous with being socially respectable.

clue.text: Scoffed feta at beano, regularly

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter, starting with the second

explanation.surface: Cheese wolfed down at a party, again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: A beano is British slang for a party or celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Scoffed is informal for eaten greedily, so consumed food is what both mean.

clue.text: Force to accept this compiler twisting proposition

indicators.note: to accept means to take in, so the word for force encloses the turned word

parts.note: to prise is to force open

indicators.note: twisting turns the setter's word round

parts.note: the compiler refers to themselves as me

explanation.surface: Someone forcing the setter to accept a contorted proposal.
explanation.definitionFit: A premise is a statement assumed as the basis of an argument, a proposition.

clue.text: Emperor about right to hold tide back

indicators.note: to hold means to contain, so the outer letters wrap around the turned word

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means about

indicators.note: back says the word for tide is read in reverse

parts.note: tide stands for the sea, as in a poetic flood of water

explanation.surface: An emperor, King Canute style, trying to hold back the tide.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls King Canute, who reputedly tried to stop the tide.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar was the title of Roman emperors, and Julius Caesar is the archetypal one.

clue.text: Warning of drink round around time

parts.note: ale is a drink of beer

indicators.note: around means the word for round surrounds the time letter

parts.note: a ring is round in shape

explanation.surface: A drinker's warning about another round coming round on time.
explanation.definitionFit: Alerting someone is warning them of danger, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Row about dodgy art for gents, perhaps

indicators.note: about means the word for row goes around the shuffled letters

parts.note: a line is a row

indicators.note: dodgy means suspect or unsound, so the letters of art are muddled

explanation.surface: A dispute over questionable art in a men's toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: The gents is British for a men's public toilet; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A gents is one type of toilet, particularly in camps or barracks called a latrine.

clue.text: Weapons and helmets for war at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of helmets for war are jumbled

explanation.surface: Arms and protective headgear for a naval battle.
explanation.definitionFit: These are weapons that project a stream of burning fuel.

clue.text: Light playing in arcade

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of in arcade are being tossed about

explanation.surface: Bright lights from the machines being played in an amusement arcade.
explanation.definitionFit: Radiance is light glowing or shining outwards, a synonym.

clue.text: Pure, natural duet moving journalist

indicators.note: moving means the letters of natural duet are put into a new order

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is the crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A pure, unaffected duet that moves a reporter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unadulterated has nothing mixed in, so it is pure.

clue.text: Coffee or tea, we hear, inside old container

indicators.note: inside puts the sound-alike letter within the word for old, which acts as the container

parts.note: late means old or former, as in the late king

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word tea is taken by its sound, a single letter

parts.note: tea said aloud is the letter T

explanation.surface: Asking whether coffee or tea is kept inside an old container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Container' just tells you that LATE (old) holds the T.
explanation.definitionFit: A latte is a coffee made with espresso and plenty of steamed milk.

clue.text: Report of frozen deluge creating vision problem

indicators.note: report of signals that the phrase is to be taken by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: a deluge of frozen precipitation is ice rain, which said aloud is close to the answer

explanation.surface: A news report about a freezing downpour causing problems with people's sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Tired, aching eyes from overuse are a common sight complaint, so this names a vision problem.

clue.text: Correct current slang for 'beggar'

parts.note: to mend is to correct or put right
I is the physics symbol for electric current
cant is jargon or slang of a particular group

explanation.surface: Fixing the current slang word for a beggar.
explanation.definitionFit: A mendicant is one who lives by begging, especially a member of an alms-seeking religious order.

clue.text: Epic poem is long. It's also dull, initially

indicators.note: initially asks for the first letter of each of the words before it

explanation.surface: A grumble that a famous epic poem is long and boring as well.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's poem of the Trojan War is the classic Greek epic.

clue.text: United trained to take on Newcastle finally …

indicators.note: to take on means to absorb something, so the word for trained holds the letter

parts.note: an animal that has been tamed has been trained

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of Newcastle

explanation.surface: A football report: Manchester United trained ahead of facing Newcastle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United' looks like a football club, but it is the definition, joined together.
explanation.definitionFit: Things teamed up are joined together, which is a synonym for united.

clue.text: Bolts sailors do on empty decks

parts.note: ABs are able seamen, so sailors
to do someone is to con or swindle them

indicators.note: empty removes the inside of decks, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: Sailors carry out their work on bare decks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bolts' looks like hardware for a ship, but it is the verb, runs away.
explanation.definitionFit: To abscond is to run off secretly, which is what one does who bolts.

clue.text: … Bury facing new wingers from Arsenal inside

indicators.note: facing means the burial word stands in front of what follows

parts.note: to inter is to bury

indicators.note: wingers are the players on the edges, so take the outer letters of Arsenal

explanation.surface: Continuing the football theme: Bury play Arsenal's wingers who cut inside.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury is a Lancashire football club, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Internal and inside both describe what lies within, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: A small room turned up around lobby — heaven!

indicators.note: around means the turned pieces surround the word for lobby
in a down clue, turned up means the pieces are read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: lav, short for lavatory, is a small room
a hall is an entrance lobby

explanation.surface: Finding a tiny room upturned around the entrance hall, and calling it heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'turned up' reads the pieces bottom to top, making VALA, which 'around' then wraps round the lobby word.
explanation.definitionFit: In Norse myth this is the hall of slain warriors, the warrior's heaven.

clue.text: Excess praise one's Queen rejected

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the joined pieces are read backwards

parts.note: to laud is to praise
one is I, and the 's stands for is
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: Too much praise for a queen being rebuffed.
explanation.definitionFit: Residual means remaining as surplus, so excess (as an adjective, left over) fits.

clue.text: Drops containing skin of elder extracts

indicators.note: containing means the word for drops holds the other piece

parts.note: dives means drops sharply

indicators.note: skin of takes the outer letters of elder

explanation.surface: Drops of elderflower extract.
explanation.definitionFit: To derive something is to obtain or extract it from a source.

clue.text: Consent from top admitting Church doctrine's first

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the word for top encloses the other pieces

parts.note: ace means top or first-rate
CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of doctrine

explanation.surface: Agreement from on high, letting in the church's chief doctrine.
explanation.definitionFit: To accede is to agree or assent to a request or demand.

clue.text: Punish Conservative over race

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: to hasten is to race or hurry

explanation.surface: Punishing a Tory politician over a race.
explanation.definitionFit: To chasten is to discipline or correct, so it means punish.

clue.text: Experts of French exercise a school head embraces

indicators.note: embraces means the outer pieces wrap around the others
head picks the first letter of school

parts.note: de is French for of
PT is physical training, exercise

explanation.surface: French experts are hugged by the head of a school.
explanation.definitionFit: Adepts are people highly skilled in something, which makes them experts.

clue.text: Suitor with reaction to innuendo

parts.note: ooer is the jokey British exclamation at a double meaning

explanation.surface: A suitor who meets a double entendre with a knowing reaction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ooer' is a British comic exclamation, mock-shocked, at a saucy remark.
explanation.definitionFit: One who courts or woos another is a suitor.

clue.text: Handy gear for relocating plant

indicators.note: relocating moves the letters of handy gear to new positions

explanation.surface: Useful tools for moving a plant in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a flowering shrub with large round heads of blooms, an example of a plant.

clue.text: Maudling ran Treasury accepting gift

indicators.note: accepting means the phrase holds the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: Reginald Maudling, as Chancellor, running the Treasury and taking a gift.
explanation.walkthrough: Reginald Maudling was a British Chancellor of the Exchequer in the 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: A grant is money given, a gift from an authority or fund.

clue.text: Improve conditions spreading deeper love endlessly

indicators.note: spreading scatters the letters of the gathered pieces into a new order
endlessly means the last letter of love is dropped

explanation.surface: Making things better by spreading ever deeper love.
explanation.definitionFit: To redevelop an area is to rebuild it and so improve conditions there.

clue.text: East River capsized craft

indicators.note: capsized means overturned, so the joined pieces are read backwards

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east
the Dart is a river in Devon, England

explanation.surface: A boat overturned on the East River in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' looks like a boat, but it is the definition in the sense of a skilled occupation.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade is a skilled occupation, so craft is a synonym.

clue.text: Kill like elite force with crime destroyed

parts.note: as means like
the SAS is the British Army's elite special forces regiment
sin is wrongdoing, loosely a crime
ate means consumed or destroyed, as in eaten away

explanation.surface: Killing in the manner of special forces, with the wrongdoing wiped out.
explanation.definitionFit: To assassinate is to kill a prominent person, usually for political reasons.
